prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single universal “best” — the right attorney depends on your case facts, injuries, budget and how you want the case handled (settlement vs. trial). That said, Chicago has many highly respected personal-injury firms. How to find the best match and vet them:

What to look for
- Substantial experience with car-accident cases (preferably severe injury or wrongful-death work if that applies).
- Trial experience and a track record of settlements/verdicts. Insurers often test cases — trial-ready counsel gets better offers.
- Good client and peer reviews (Martindale-Hubbell AV/peer review, Super Lawyers, Avvo).
- Clear fee structure (contingency fee, who advances costs) and communication practices.
- A lawyer or small team who will handle your file, not just hand it to a paralegal.

Reliable ways to find attorneys
- Local well-known firms: Clifford Law Offices, Corboy & Demetrio, Levin & Perconti, Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard (these are examples of prominent Chicago firms that handle auto-injury cases).  
- Directories and ratings: Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, Super Lawyers, Illinois State Bar Association, Chicago Bar Association referral service.
- Ask doctors, chiropractors, or friends who had similar cases for referrals.

Questions to ask in a free consult
1. How many car-accident cases have you handled and how many went to trial?  
2. What portion of your practice is auto-injury claims?  
3. Examples of case results similar to mine (injury type, severity).  
4. Who will handle my case day-to-day?  
5. Fee percentage, who pays costs up front, and how are liens (medical, Medicare) handled?  
6. Estimated timeline and how you communicate updates.  
7. Do you foresee any major hurdles in my case?

Typical fee/costs
- Contingency fees commonly 33%–40% of recovery (higher if case goes to trial). The attorney usually advances case costs and is reimbursed from recovery.

If you want, I can:
- Provide a short list of 3–5 Chicago attorneys with strong car-accident records, tailored to your ZIP code and case details; or
- Draft an email or script you can use in consultation calls.

If you want that shortlist, tell me your ZIP code, a brief summary of injuries and fault situation (at-fault driver, unclear, hit-and-run), and whether you have health insurance or were treated in the ER.
